messages:
lia: Quick follow-up from the model-format sync — thinking about a tiny metadata-first path for weights so cold-starts avoid scanning giant safetensors blobs.
kevin: +1. can you sketch the invariants you want? start-up latency is the main win, right?
sam: Also want to know how this plays with sharded uploads and our existing shard manifest format.
lia: Goals: 1) no change to user-facing tensor files (safetensors remain unchanged). 2) small index file (<=100KB) that lists tensor offsets, dtype, shape, shard id. 3) loader can mmap/zero-copy payloads when available. 4) warmup can request a "hotset" of offsets.
sabrina: so index file => .widx or .sindex? prefer descriptive extension so S3 lifecycle rules can match.
kevin: .widx sounds fine. important: it must be optional fallback to scanning the safetensors if absent.
sam: agree. for sharded models, index should point at shard URI + byte range. that avoids adding a bundle format.
lia: sketch of manifest snippet:
```
{
  "version": 1,
  "tensors": [
    {"name":"transformer.w1","dtype":"f16","shape":[12288,4096],"shard":"shard-000","offset":12345},
    ...
  ],
  "hotset_hints": ["transformer.w1","transformer.attn_kv"]
}
```
kevin: Hotset hints are good. runtime can prefetch hotset into GPU/DRAM with separate priority queue.
sabrina: Q: how to keep index consistent with safetensors if someone re-uploads? version+checksum pair in index header?
lia: yes include sha256 of the underlying shard objects and a manifest-level version. loader must verify checksum on first open (cheap streaming hash), otherwise fall back to conservative behavior.
kevin: Another tradeoff: if we mmap a shard on NFS / remote FUSE, page faults are expensive. We should prefer an explicit read path with async prefetch for non-local stores.
sam: we already have a read-through cache layer. maybe loader picks strategy by storage class: local->mmap, remote->aio-read with read-ahead.
weights-bot: deploy job queued: weights-indexer v2 -> canary
lia: Perf numbers from my local sim: index-first + hotset prefetch reduces 95p init from ~1.8s to ~240ms on 7B-like model when hotset <= 15 tensors.
sabrina: nice. does this change our warmup API? I think WarmupManager.request_hotset(model, list[string]) where list is names or regex.
kevin: Also expose a budget (bytes or time) for warmup e.g. request_hotset(..., budget_bytes=64MB) so caller can cap cost.
lia: Implementation plan: (1) add optional .widx generation in our bundler and uploaders; (2) extend WeightSource abstraction to accept index blobs; (3) WarmupManager uses index to create prioritized download plan; (4) fallback: when index missing, scanner produces ephemeral index (slower).
sam: backward compatibility: if we can't produce .widx for older models, run ephemeral scan but persist generated index in cache for next start.
kevin: security: index must not leak extra metadata. only expose tensors names and offsets. checksum prevents tampering.
sabrina: follow-ups: small RFC for index layout + s3 object mapping and eviction heuristics. I can draft.
lia: cool. I'll open the RFC and link perf microbench. who wants to own index writer in bundler? @kevin?
kevin: i'll take writer + integration tests.
sam: i'll wire loader + storage strategy switch.
lia: thanks. +:thumbsup: this should give big startup wins without forcing format changes.
weights-bot: deploy job started: weights-indexer v2 -> canary
kevin: filing task in phab, ping when RFC is up.
sabrina: ack, will watch for RFC.
